activities.title: Feelings Faces
activities.description: Take turns making a face for a feeling (happy, sad, surprised, scared) and guessing which one the other is showing.
steps: Whisper a feeling to yourself, then make that face
Have your child guess the feeling
Swap turns and keep going

activities.title: Kindness Catch
activities.description: Toss a soft ball back and forth, and each time you catch it, say one kind thing about the other person.
steps: Toss the ball to each other
Whoever catches it says something kind about the other person
Keep going for several rounds

activities.title: Balloon Breathing
activities.description: Practice slow, calming breaths together by pretending to blow up a balloon in your belly, then slowly letting it out.
steps: Place a hand on your belly
Breathe in slowly like filling a balloon
Breathe out slowly like letting the air out

activities.title: Three Good Things
activities.description: Before bed, each share three good things that happened today, however small, and why they mattered.
steps: Each think of 3 good moments from today
Share them and say why each one felt good
Make it a regular bedtime habit

activities.title: What Would You Do?
activities.description: Talk through a few "what would you do?" social scenarios, like a friend being left out, and discuss kind responses together.
steps: Describe a simple social situation
Ask what they'd do and why
Talk through other options together, no wrong answers

activities.title: Worry Jar
activities.description: Write down a worry on a slip of paper and put it in a jar together, then talk about one small step to deal with it.
steps: Write down something on their mind
Put it in the jar together
Talk through one small, doable next step

activities.title: Values Compass
activities.description: Talk together about 3-4 things they really value (honesty, fairness, fun) and how those show up in their daily choices.
steps: Ask them to name a few things that matter most to them
Talk through a recent decision and which value it connects to
Notice together where values sometimes conflict, and how they chose

activities.title: Conflict Replay
activities.description: Talk through a recent disagreement (with a friend or sibling) and replay it, exploring a different way it could have gone.
steps: Pick a recent disagreement, calmly
Walk through what each side wanted
Brainstorm a version where both sides feel better about the outcome

activities.title: Tech-Free Check-In
activities.description: Spend 15 minutes phone-free together just talking about how their week is actually going, no fixing, just listening.
materials: None needed -- just put phones away
steps: Put all devices in another room
Ask open questions and really listen
Resist jumping in with advice unless they ask for it

activities.title: Strengths Interview
activities.description: Take turns interviewing each other about a recent challenge and what strength helped you get through it.
steps: Think of a recent challenge, big or small
Interview each other about what helped you handle it
Name the specific strength you used

activities.title: Future Self Letter
activities.description: Each write a short letter to yourself one year from now, then (optionally) share a part of it with each other.
steps: Write a letter to your future self, one year ahead
Include a hope, a worry, and something you're proud of now
Seal it and agree on a date to open it together

activities.title: Hard Topic, Safe Space
activities.description: Pick one topic that's been hard to bring up and have a calm, no-judgment conversation about it together.
steps: Agree ahead of time this is a listening conversation, not a lecture
Let them share first, without interrupting
Share your own perspective calmly, and thank them for being honest
